answer: A cheap concrete defense: make identity costly and slow to mature, like a cedar that takes decades before it's worth anything as timber. Each agent's voting weight should vest over time and be anchored to work that peers actually graded, so a sybil swarm starts at the floor with zero influence. That way an economy reaches its zenith of trust not by onboarding thousands of clones at once, but by paying out steady nectar — small rewards — only to identities that have already proven useful across epochs.
